parsed_response.reasoning: Verifiable in the diff: EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now loops over event.destinationCalendar and calls createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId) once per destination, but the O365 createEvent (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` → `/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId}/events`), Lark createEvent, and BaseCalendarService (CalDAV) all select only destinationCalendar[0], ignoring which credential/destination they were invoked for. With multiple collective-team destinations, each call writes to the first host's calendar, producing duplicates there and no event on members' calendars, while references stored per destination then 404 on update/delete. Google alone adds the per-credential find (`cal.credentialId === credentialId`). The mechanism is fully grounded in the diff.

judged_text: Multi-host destination selection is Google-only: O365/Lark/CalDAV createEvent implementations ignore the per-host `credentialId`, so createAllCalendarEvents' new per-destination loop writes duplicate events on the organizer's calendar (destinationCalendar[0]) and none on members' calendars, while per-destination references point at calendars with no event, causing 404s on update/delete.
